components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main action button with cyan accent. Used for primary CTAs.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: rgba(78, 205, 196, 0.2); color: #4ecdc4; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(78, 205, 196, 0.5); border-radius: 8px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(78, 205, 196, 0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4ecdc4; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action button with subtle hover state.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #888888; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #4ecdc4; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Dark input field with cyan focus border.
components.css: .ds-input { background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3); color: #e0e0ff; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(78, 205, 196, 0.2); border-radius: 8px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; width: 100%; transition: border-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgba(136, 136, 136, 0.5); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: rgba(78, 205, 196, 0.5); outline: none; }

components.name: Glass Panel
components.description: Floating glass container for content sections.
components.css: .ds-glass-panel { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); backdrop-filter: blur(10px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(10px); border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1); border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1); } .ds-glass-panel h3 { color: #4ecdc4; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; margin: 0 0 12px 0; } .ds-glass-panel p { color: #e0e0ff; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; margin: 0; }

narrative.overview:
ZedFace is not a chatbot wrapper. It is a neural interface — a direct cognitive link between developer and AI. The design system reflects this: every element exists to minimize friction in the thought-to-action pipeline. The interface dissolves, leaving only the collaboration.

The system is precise — every pixel has purpose, every animation communicates state. It is immersive — full-screen, edge-to-edge, eliminating the browser frame to create a dedicated cognitive space. It is geeky — unapologetically technical, celebrating the aesthetic of development tools. It is futuristic — not science fiction fantasy, but near-future reality, the interface you'd expect in 2030.
keyCharacteristics: Particle system as AI identity (not decoration)
Exponential easing for all motion (no bounce, no elastic)
Cyan-magenta duality: calm intelligence + urgent energy
Full-screen immersion with floating UI layers

rules.name: The Signal Clarity Rule
rules.body: Primary cyan appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. When everything is highlighted, nothing is.

rules.name: The Duality Doctrine
rules.body: Cyan and magenta are never mixed decoratively. Cyan = thought/interface. Magenta = action/urgency. They coexist, but never blur.

rules.name: The Prose Boundary Rule
rules.body: Body text never exceeds 75 characters per line. Controlled via max-width: 65ch. Long lines fatigue the eye; short lines waste space. 65-75ch is the sweet spot.

rules.name: The Mono Isolation Rule
rules.body: Technical content (code, logs, data) uses JetBrains Mono. Never mix monospace and sans-serif in the same semantic unit. The visual break signals 'this is machine-generated.'

rules.name: The Functional Glass Rule
rules.body: Glassmorphism is structural, not decorative. Use it for floating panels, modals, overlays — elements that exist above the particle background. Never use it for static cards, list items, or form fields. If the element doesn't float, it doesn't need glass.

rules.name: The Blur Budget Rule
rules.body: Standard blur is 10px. Subtle is 8px. Strong is 12px. Never exceed 12px — too much blur destroys legibility and kills performance. The background should be discernible, not obliterated.

dos: Do use glassmorphism for floating panels and overlays — elements that exist above the particle background.
Do maintain cyan as the primary signal color, used on ≤10% of any surface. Its rarity is its power.
Do use exponential easing (ease-out-expo, ease-in-out-expo) for all transitions. No bounce, no elastic.
Do keep body text line length at 65-75 characters. Use max-width: 65ch on content containers.
Do use JetBrains Mono for all technical content (code, logs, data).
Do provide prefers-reduced-motion alternatives without eliminating feedback.
Do maintain WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and UI components.
donts: Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. If the element doesn't float above the background, it doesn't need glass.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent (side-stripe border anti-pattern).
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient background). This is decorative, never meaningful.
Don't create enterprise admin dashboard layouts (Salesforce, SAP style).
Don't use consumer chat application patterns (WeChat, Messenger style).
Don't overuse magenta. It signals urgency and danger. Reserve it for warnings, errors, and destructive actions.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing. Motion should feel physical and precise.
Don't create identical card grids with icon + heading + text repeated endlessly.
Don't reduce or remove animations without providing alternatives.
Don't use #000 or #fff. Tint every neutral toward the brand hue.
